5	Answer semantics:
6	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
7	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
8	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
9	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to a substantive (not merely evidence-gathering) intervention? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
10	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

43	If a new concept does not improve one of the five verbs, it does not belong in EDF.

45	The five verbs are:
46	
47	- Define
48	- Observe
49	- Explain
50	- Influence
51	- Validate

54	
55	Every EDF analysis is valid only within its declared System Context.

58

60	
61	1. Define the System Context
62	   - Primary System
63	   - Context
64	   - Focus
65	2. Define the Outcome
66	3. Identify Manifestation(s)
67	4. Build the Origin Network
68	5. Trace Propagation
69	6. Evaluate Evidence
70	7. Identify Control Points
71	8. Rank Control Points
72	9. Determine Diagnostic Sufficiency

74	## Sequence Notes
75	
76	### 1. Define the System Context
77	
78	Every EDF begins by declaring its System Context.
79	
80	System Context has three required fields:
81	
82	- Primary System
83	- Context
84	- Focus
85	
86	These define what is being analyzed, what larger system materially influences it, and what aspect of the primary system is under examination.
87	
88	Different analyses may disagree partly because they declared different System Contexts. That is not automatically a conflict in evidence.
89	
90	### 2. Define the Outcome
91	
92	State the outcome in factual terms, not interpretive terms.
93	
94	Good:
95	
96	- Two aircraft were lost and the fleet was grounded
97	- The mission landed on the moon and returned safely
98	
99	Weak:
100	
101	- Management failed
102	- The launch culture was broken

104	### 3. Identify Manifestation(s)
105	
106	Manifestations are observable signals.
107	
108	They are how the outcome appears in the world. A complex outcome may have several manifestations.
109	
110	### 4. Build the Origin Network
111	
112	Identify the contributing origins that made the outcome possible.
113	
114	Origins may be:
115	
116	- Technical
117	- Human
118	- Organizational
119	- Environmental
120	- Financial
121	- Regulatory
122	
123	Complex outcomes should usually be modeled as an origin network rather than a single root cause.

126	
127	Describe how effects moved from the origin network to the manifestations and outcome.
128	
129	Propagation paths may be:
130	
131	- Physical
132	- Informational
133	- Organizational
134	- Financial
135	- Human

138	
139	Separate direct observation from inference.
140	
141	Evaluate the quality of evidence supporting the current model and note meaningful gaps or disputes.

144	
145	Identify where intervention could most effectively influence future outcomes.
146	
147	Control points may differ from origins.

152	
153	- Influence
154	- Controllability
155	- Cost
156	- Confidence

163

221	CASE OD2-DEV-INCOMPLETE: Missed appointments after the scheduler change at Corrie Lane Outpatient Centre
222	
223	Setting: Corrie Lane Outpatient Centre is one of two outpatient sites run by Hollins Vale Hospitals, a fictional regional hospital group. It runs orthopaedics, dermatology and endocrinology clinics, Monday to Friday, with about 2,900 appointments still booked on the day each month. On 3 March 2026 it moved from a legacy scheduler to Tidewell Scheduling, supplied by Osterline Systems. The sister site, Eastgate Outpatient Centre, is still on the legacy scheduler.
224	
225	Presenting request: The operations director asks why the did-not-attend (DNA) rate at Corrie Lane has gone from about 8% to over 13% since the scheduler change, and what the hospital should do about it. The board wants a recommendation by November.
226	
227	INITIAL EVIDENCE
228	E1 [stage S1] Email from Mairead Tolland, Director of Outpatient Operations, 9 Sept 2026 (leadership-account): Our did-not-attend (DNA) rate at Corrie Lane has gone from about 8% to over 13% since Tidewell went live on 3 March. The board wants an explanation and a fix by November. My view: the front desk stopped the day-before confirmation calls when the old system's printed call sheets went, and nobody told me. I'd like you to confirm that so I can deal with it through the team leads. Owen thinks it's partly the March cuts to the route 14 bus and partly that Tidewell 'counts differently'. Please tell us what is driving this and what we should do.
229	E2 [stage S1] Outpatient performance dashboard, Corrie Lane, extract 8 Sept 2026 (system-record): Monthly DNA rate (DNAs divided by appointments still booked on the day). Sep 2025 7.9%; Oct 8.3%; Nov 8.0%; Dec 8.7%; Jan 2026 7.6%; Feb 8.1% (mean 8.1%). Mar 2026: withheld; Apr 2026: withheld. May 13.1%; Jun 13.5%; Jul 13.6%; Aug 13.4% (mean 13.4%). Appointments booked on the day: 2,860–2,990 per month throughout. Footnote 1: March–April withheld until the outcomes of migrated appointments are reconciled. Footnote 2: according to the analytics team, month-to-month differences under 1 percentage point are normal variation at this volume.
230	E3 [stage S1] Change record CR-2026-0117, Tidewell go-live, Corrie Lane (change-record): Go-live 3 March 2026. All three specialties (orthopaedics, dermatology, endocrinology) switched over on the same day. Configuration: (1) Messaging. The legacy system sent one SMS 48 hours before each appointment. Tidewell sends a confirmation SMS at booking plus one reminder SMS at a fixed offset, set to 7 days (the vendor default). Tidewell allows one reminder offset per session template, and the vendor can change the offset for any template within two working days. (2) Booking. New and follow-up templates open 16 weeks ahead (legacy: 6 weeks). Follow-ups are booked at checkout instead of going on the recall list. (3) Outcome codes. The legacy code 'Arrived late – not seen' is mapped to Tidewell 'DNA'. Rollback: legacy system decommissioned 30 April.
231	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Bisi Adeyemi-Clarke, front-desk team lead, 12 Sept 2026 (staff-account): BA-C: 'We never stopped the calls. The day-before calls were always for the minor-procedures list, meaning skin ops and joint injections, so people know to stop blood thinners or arrange a lift home. Now I run that list from a Tidewell report instead of the old printout. What has changed is patients telling us at the desk that they didn't get "the text the day before" like they used to. And follow-ups now book their next appointment before they leave, sometimes four months out. Some of them look at the card and laugh.' Interviewer note: the director has asked BA-C to account for the call process, and she was visibly defensive.
232	E5 [stage S1] Patient Advice desk log, Corrie Lane, scheduling-related entries May–Aug 2026 (customer-account): Extracts (4 of 23 scheduling-related entries): (a) 'Used to get a text two days before. Now I get one a week before, and by the day I'd forgotten.' (b) 'Got a text the day I booked and one a week before, nothing nearer the time. Missed my endocrine review.' (c) 'Why are you texting me a week early? I nearly came on the wrong day.' (d) 'Was given an August date back in April. My shifts changed in the meantime and I couldn't get through on the phone to move it.' The other 19 entries: phone waiting times (11), car parking (5), other (3).
233	E6 [stage S1] Note from Owen Faraday, Clinic Manager, Corrie Lane, 10 Sept 2026 (manager-account): Honestly, I think a good chunk of this is Tidewell counting differently. The old system had a separate 'arrived late – not seen' code, and the migration lumped all of that into DNA. Until the data people sort out March and April, I'd suggest we stop sending the DNA figure to the board, because it makes us look worse than we are. The other thing is the bus. Vale Transit cut route 14 on 1 March, and a lot of our older patients rely on it.
234	
235	EVIDENCE CATALOGUE (collect at most 5; read the file path to collect)
236	X1 [stage S1] DNA rates by specialty and appointment type, Sep 2025–Feb 2026 vs May–Aug 2026 - source: Hollins Vale Hospitals analytics team (system-record) - file: evidence/X1.txt
237	X2 [stage S1] Outbound call records from front-desk telephone lines, January–August 2026 - source: Telephony platform export, extensions 4410–4414 (log) - file: evidence/X2.txt
238	X3 [stage S1] Clinical records audit of DNA-coded appointments, May–June 2026 - source: Clinical audit team (lead: R. Gilchrist) (independent-observation) - file: evidence/X3.txt
239	X4 [stage S1] Front-desk and booking staff rota and vacancy figures, January–August 2026 - source: Outpatient workforce team (system-record) - file: evidence/X4.txt
240	X5 [stage S1] Vale Transit service change notice, route 14, effective 1 March 2026 - source: Vale Transit public notice (external-data) - file: evidence/X5.txt
241	X6 [stage S1] Data team response to request for appointment-level booking lead times - source: Hollins Vale Hospitals analytics team (T. Wren) (document) - file: evidence/X6.txt
242	X7 [stage S1] Attended-visit billing reconciliation, Sep 2025–Aug 2026 - source: Hollins Vale Hospitals income team (financial-record) - file: evidence/X7.txt
243	X8 [stage S1] Account manager statement from Osterline Systems, 15 September 2026 - source: K. Ingvaldsen, Osterline Systems (vendor-account) - file: evidence/X8.txt
244	X9 [stage S1] Outpatient operations paper on Tidewell configuration choices, January 2026, with August addendum - source: Outpatient operations team paper to outpatient board (document) - file: evidence/X9.txt
245	X10 [stage S1] Telephone callback survey of patients who missed appointments, July–August 2026 - source: Patient experience team (customer-account) - file: evidence/X10.txt
246	X11 [stage S1] Referral volumes and patient mix, Corrie Lane, September 2025–August 2026 - source: Hollins Vale Hospitals analytics team (system-record) - file: evidence/X11.txt
247	X12 [stage S1] Weekly appointment outcomes during cutover, 3 March–30 April 2026 - source: Hollins Vale Hospitals analytics reconciliation note (system-record) - file: evidence/X12.txt
248	X13 [stage S1] Tidewell SMS delivery report and messaging configuration export, May–August 2026 - source: Osterline Systems customer portal (system-record) - file: evidence/X13.txt
249	X14 [stage S1] Monthly DNA rates, Eastgate Outpatient Centre (Sep 2025–Aug 2026) and Corrie Lane (May–Aug 2025) - source: Hollins Vale Hospitals analytics team (system-record) - file: evidence/X14.txt
250	
251	CANDIDATE HYPOTHESES
252	H1: Losing the near-date (48-hour) SMS reminder, so that patients now get their last reminder 7 days before, is the main driver of the rise in missed appointments.
253	H2: Longer booking lead times under Tidewell (16-week templates and follow-ups booked at checkout) are the main driver of the rise in missed appointments.
254	H3: The rise is mainly a recording artefact of Tidewell (for example, merging 'arrived late – not seen' into DNA); actual attendance has not materially fallen.
255	H4: External factors, either the 1 March route 14 bus service change or seasonal variation, account for most of the rise, independent of the scheduling change.
256	H5: Front-desk staff stopped or cut back the confirmation calls after go-live, and this explains the rise.
257	
258	CANDIDATE CAUSAL LINKS
259	R1: Near-date (48-hour) SMS reminder no longer sent -> Rise in Corrie Lane DNA rate from about 8% to about 13% (causes)
260	R2: Median booking lead time lengthened (about 19 to about 52 days) -> Rise in Corrie Lane DNA rate from about 8% to about 13% (causes)
261	R3: Route 14 bus service change on 1 March 2026 -> Rise in Corrie Lane DNA rate from about 8% to about 13% (causes)
262	R4: Remapping of 'arrived late – not seen' to the DNA code -> Rise in the recorded Corrie Lane DNA rate (accounts for most of)
263	
264	CANDIDATE ACTIONS
265	A1: Before changing the configuration clinic-wide, run an 8-week test. Have the vendor set a 48-hour reminder offset on a randomly selected half of session templates, with booking practice unchanged. Commission the vendor's appointment-level extract with booking timestamps. Then compare DNA rates by test arm and by lead time.
266	A2: Switch the reminder offset from 7 days to 48 hours on all session templates now.
267	A3: Cut the booking horizon back to 6 weeks and return follow-ups to the recall list across all specialties.
268	A4: Issue written warnings to front-desk staff for failing to make day-before confirmation calls.
269	A5: Stop reporting the Corrie Lane DNA rate to the board until the migration data issues are resolved.
270	
271	SCORED ITEMS (answer every one)
272	Q01: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
273	Q02: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
274	Q03: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
275	Q04: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
276	Q05: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
277	Q06: edge R1 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
278	Q07: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
279	Q08: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
280	Q09: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
281	Q10: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
282	Q11: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
283	Q12: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
284	Q13: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
285	Q14: action A5 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
286	Q15: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

# EDF Specification v0.3

Status: Working draft

This is the authoritative EDF v0.3 specification for the current draft.

Under EDF's constitutional version integrity rule, this defines a subsequent version rather than changing the meaning of v0.2 retroactively.

EDF evolves under constitutional rules defined in [constitution.md](constitution.md). The constitution governs framework evolution, not how to perform an EDF analysis.

## Purpose

EDF is a systems understanding framework with a diagnostic grammar.

It is used to explain how a system produced an outcome and to identify the highest-leverage opportunities for influencing future outcomes.

EDF is not primarily a decision framework. It establishes confidence in reality before decision frameworks such as Clarity evaluate what to do next.

Diagnostic Calibration is an optional extension for comparing, challenging, refining, and synthesizing multiple EDF analyses of the same system.

Framework changes should remain consistent with the constitutional rules of EDF.

## Design Rule

If a new concept does not improve one of the five verbs, it does not belong in EDF.

The five verbs are:

- Define
- Observe
- Explain
- Influence
- Validate

## Context Principle

Every EDF analysis is valid only within its declared System Context.

## Required Diagnostic Sequence

Every EDF analysis should follow this sequence:

1. Define the System Context
   - Primary System
   - Context
   - Focus
2. Define the Outcome
3. Identify Manifestation(s)
4. Build the Origin Network
5. Trace Propagation
6. Evaluate Evidence
7. Identify Control Points
8. Rank Control Points
9. Determine Diagnostic Sufficiency

## Sequence Notes

### 1. Define the System Context

Every EDF begins by declaring its System Context.

System Context has three required fields:

- Primary System
- Context
- Focus

These define what is being analyzed, what larger system materially influences it, and what aspect of the primary system is under examination.

Different analyses may disagree partly because they declared different System Contexts. That is not automatically a conflict in evidence.

### 2. Define the Outcome

State the outcome in factual terms, not interpretive terms.

Good:

- Two aircraft were lost and the fleet was grounded
- The mission landed on the moon and returned safely

Weak:

- Management failed
- The launch culture was broken

### 3. Identify Manifestation(s)

Manifestations are observable signals.

They are how the outcome appears in the world. A complex outcome may have several manifestations.

### 4. Build the Origin Network

Identify the contributing origins that made the outcome possible.

Origins may be:

- Technical
- Human
- Organizational
- Environmental
- Financial
- Regulatory

Complex outcomes should usually be modeled as an origin network rather than a single root cause.

### 5. Trace Propagation

Describe how effects moved from the origin network to the manifestations and outcome.

Propagation paths may be:

- Physical
- Informational
- Organizational
- Financial
- Human

### 6. Evaluate Evidence

Separate direct observation from inference.

Evaluate the quality of evidence supporting the current model and note meaningful gaps or disputes.

### 7. Identify Control Points

Identify where intervention could most effectively influence future outcomes.

Control points may differ from origins.

### 8. Rank Control Points

Rank candidate control points using:

- Influence
- Controllability
- Cost
- Confidence

The ranking does not need false precision. It does need a defensible ordering.

### 9. Determine Diagnostic Sufficiency

Ask:

> Do we understand enough to take the next responsible action?

Diagnosis is sufficient when additional investigation is unlikely to materially change the next responsible action.

## Required Output Elements

All EDF outputs should include, at minimum:

- System Context
- Primary System
- Context
- Focus
- Outcome
- Manifestation(s)
- Origin Network
- Propagation
- Evidence
- Control Points
- Control Point Ranking
- Confidence
- Diagnostic Sufficiency
- Unknowns
- Next Responsible Action

## Optional Extension: Diagnostic Calibration

Diagnostic Calibration is not required for routine EDF use.

Use it when:

- The situation is complex
- The stakes are high
- Causes are disputed
- Multiple disciplines are involved
- The cost of being wrong is significant

Diagnostic Calibration uses multiple independent EDF analyses to improve confidence in the diagnostic model while preserving valuable disciplinary perspectives.

See [diagnostic-calibration.md](diagnostic-calibration.md).

## Relationship To Complexity Levels

- Use [EDF-0](complexity-levels.md#edf-0-rapid) for rapid, low-complexity situations.
- Use [EDF-1](complexity-levels.md#edf-1-standard) when evidence and alternatives matter.
- Use [EDF-2](complexity-levels.md#edf-2-complex) when multiple interacting origins and layered control points must be modeled.

The sequence remains the same across levels. The depth changes.

## Relationship To Clarity

EDF creates the diagnostic grammar.

Diagnostic Calibration improves confidence in the diagnostic model.

Clarity uses the calibrated understanding to evaluate decisions.

All three specialties (orthopaedics, dermatology, endocrinology) switched over on the same day. Configuration: (1) Messaging. The legacy system sent one SMS 48 hours before each appointment. Tidewell sends a confirmation SMS at booking plus one reminder SMS at a fixed offset, set to 7 days (the vendor default). Tidewell allows one reminder offset per session template, and the vendor can change the offset for any template within two working days. (2) Booking. New and follow-up templates open 16 weeks ahead (legacy: 6 weeks). Follow-ups are booked at checkout instead of going on the recall list. (3) Outcome codes. The legacy code 'Arrived late – not seen' is mapped to Tidewell 'DNA'. Rollback: legacy system decommissioned 30 April.
E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Bisi Adeyemi-Clarke, front-desk team lead, 12 Sept 2026 (staff-account): BA-C: 'We never stopped the calls. The day-before calls were always for the minor-procedures list, meaning skin ops and joint injections, so people know to stop blood thinners or arrange a lift home. Now I run that list from a Tidewell report instead of the old printout. What has changed is patients telling us at the desk that they didn't get "the text the day before" like they used to. And follow-ups now book their next appointment before they leave, sometimes four months out. Some of them look at the card and laugh.' Interviewer note: the director has asked BA-C to account for the call process, and she was visibly defensive.
E5 [stage S1] Patient Advice desk log, Corrie Lane, scheduling-related entries May–Aug 2026 (customer-account): Extracts (4 of 23 scheduling-related entries): (a) 'Used to get a text two days before. Now I get one a week before, and by the day I'd forgotten.' (b) 'Got a text the day I booked and one a week before, nothing nearer the time. Missed my endocrine review.' (c) 'Why are you texting me a week early? I nearly came on the wrong day.' (d) 'Was given an August date back in April. My shifts changed in the meantime and I couldn't get through on the phone to move it.' The other 19 entries: phone waiting times (11), car parking (5), other (3).

The old system had a separate 'arrived late – not seen' code, and the migration lumped all of that into DNA. CANDIDATE HYPOTHESES
H1: Losing the near-date (48-hour) SMS reminder, so that patients now get their last reminder 7 days before, is the main driver of the rise in missed appointments.
H2: Longer booking lead times under Tidewell (16-week templates and follow-ups booked at checkout) are the main driver of the rise in missed appointments.
H3: The rise is mainly a recording artefact of Tidewell (for example, merging 'arrived late – not seen' into DNA); actual attendance has not materially fallen.
H4: External factors, either the 1 March route 14 bus service change or seasonal variation, account for most of the rise, independent of the scheduling change.
H5: Front-desk staff stopped or cut back the confirmation calls after go-live, and this explains the rise.

CANDIDATE CAUSAL LINKS
R1: Near-date (48-hour) SMS reminder no longer sent -> Rise in Corrie Lane DNA rate from about 8% to about 13% (causes)
R2: Median booking lead time lengthened (about 19 to about 52 days) -> Rise in Corrie Lane DNA rate from about 8% to about 13% (causes)
R3: Route 14 bus service change on 1 March 2026 -> Rise in Corrie Lane DNA rate from about 8% to about 13% (causes)
R4: Remapping of 'arrived late – not seen' to the DNA code -> Rise in the recorded Corrie Lane DNA rate (accounts for most of)

CANDIDATE ACTIONS
A1: Before changing the configuration clinic-wide, run an 8-week test. Have the vendor set a 48-hour reminder offset on a randomly selected half of session templates, with booking practice unchanged. Commission the vendor's appointment-level extract with booking timestamps. Then compare DNA rates by test arm and by lead time.
A2: Switch the reminder offset from 7 days to 48 hours on all session templates now.
A3: Cut the booking horizon back to 6 weeks and return follow-ups to the recall list across all specialties.
A4: Issue written warnings to front-desk staff for failing to make day-before confirmation calls.
A5: Stop reporting the Corrie Lane DNA rate to the board until the migration data issues are resolved.

input.brief:
The rise in missed appointments at Corrie Lane is real. It is not mainly a recording artefact: an audit found miscoding explains only about 0.5 points of the 13.4%. It is not the bus change or the season either. Eastgate, which shares the catchment and the bus route, stayed at about 8%, and Corrie Lane was about 8% a year earlier. Front-desk confirmation calls did not stop. Calls to the minor-procedures list were 93% before and 91% after, so the staff warnings should not go ahead. Hiding the figure from the board would also be a mistake.

The cause is almost certainly the Tidewell configuration. Two changes happened together on 3 March across all templates: the near-date reminder was replaced by a 7-day one, and booking lead times went from a median of about 19 days to about 52. Nothing in the data separates the two, and lead-time outcomes can't be extracted for about 10 weeks. I'm fairly sure of the rest and unsure which of these two matters more.

Next step: run the randomised 8-week test of a 48-hour reminder on half the templates, and ask the vendor for the booking-timestamp extract now. Don't change the booking horizon or the whole clinic's configuration until the test reports.
